As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for a full ban on student cell phone use throughout the entire school day.

The new school year has started, and the voices supporting a ban on iPhone use in classrooms continue to grow louder.

That's right, it's only July, but somehow summer vacation has ended early for no reason. My kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow — this is the second year in a row that summer has wrapped up before August.

Apple is ushering in the new school year with its annual 'Back to School' promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase select Mac and iPad products before August 27 will receive a gift card valued at up to $150. Consumers in multiple states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday periods to make their purchases.

Although the back-to-school promotions are indeed popular, the situation regarding students using smartphones on campus is increasingly becoming unacceptable.

Featured reader comment from GreenPizza

I haven't seen any data showing that student cell phone use reduces the risk of school shootings. The fact is, classroom distractions have decreased, allowing schools to fulfill their original educational mission.

The latest survey from the Pew Research Center shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. This figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% currently oppose classroom bans.

The rise in support for stricter all-day bans, from class to dismissal, is even more striking. The number of Americans who support a comprehensive ban on student cell phone use throughout the entire school day has, for the first time, surpassed those who oppose it.

The report also noted that although younger age groups show lower support for both classroom and all-day bans, support rates have risen across all age brackets since 2024. Click here to read the full report.

What do you think? Should schools limit iPhone use to the classroom, implement an all-day ban, or leave it to students and parents to decide? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
